title: Bound physical component precision for the corrected P104 dual
body:
PR2586 leaves the physical component precision of its corrected P104 inverse-transpose open. This source-bound successor proves a sufficient format at every instruction boundary and every positive payload tensor depth `lambda`:

- extra fractional bits: `max(10*lambda, 9*lambda+2)`;
- component magnitude: `< H*2^(ceil((9*lambda+1)/2)+6)`.

A new exact transient shows why endpoint-only precision fails. Integer product-delta input Y2 reaches `-(1-i)^lambda / 2^(5*lambda+2)` in D18 after event 2143, requiring `ceil(9*lambda/2)+2` fractional bits; its complete final state requires exactly one fewer bit. At one layer this is `(-1+i)/128` internally versus six fractional bits at the endpoint.

The separate rational and reverse interpreters check the literal frame/invoice ledger and finite proof premises. A direct Gaussian-integer array interpreter executes all 5,398 events for the stated physical input, including all eight private erasures. Retained source bytes are authenticated; no predecessor executable is imported. The unchanged construction, rank mass 3542 and logical P=127/2 retain predecessor credit.

Scope: exact atomic instructions in canonical charts. The format is conservative. Child-internal precision, approximate errors, rounded strict-zero erasure, intrinsic adapters, routing/hosting, idle/residual costs and supplier admission remain open. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

Base: current main `b4560d9e7216f72b73c5aa940ac099c05e33ccf9`, priority revision 5. Audited PR2586 head: `7953c9a8f788a8de5cf2ced63d9a61b67c22c6f1`. Contribution: `aeb5551b162b78e33c0b42681abaff92eb608d70`. Only `research/p104-physical-dual-grid/` is added, with task card, written proof, exact inputs, receipt, open questions and registered replay.

Validation on CPython 3.12.14/macOS arm64:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-physical-dual-grid
python3.12 -I -O -B research/p104-physical-dual-grid/verify.py
python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'
git diff --cached --check
```

Passed: registered replay, four behavioral groups, five semantic controls, Git-free optimized export, real source/typed-receipt corruption and chart unitarity/inversion; repository suite ran 65 tests with three skips. Native compiler regeneration, selected cold replay, proof-assistant and hosted CI were not run.

[Canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2649). Final fully paginated overlap: 840 open PRs and 1,305 Discussion records, no warnings. James Reed's Discussion2644 covers logical replay and excludes physical precision; PR2662 and Discussions2646/2647 change the word or endpoint convention and are outside this theorem.

Credit ywz65/PR2586/2497, PR2551's boundary/witness, Nick Petalas/PR2550/2549, Adam Gall/PR2096, the PR2603 component-grid precedent, and the complete retained P104/native/geometry/correction lineage in the README and byte-identical predecessor notice. Prepared for Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. No independent human or maintainer review claimed.
